exploit_wave_CF.name: wave-CF — the CALL-FORWARD marker plan (the 9th whole-body marker plan)
exploit_wave_CF.why: `plan_operand_marker_temps`'s `operands_of` has no `Inst::Call` arm, so EVERY body containing a call is outside the operand-temp class; the wave-8a forward then passes the parameter place straight in with `move`, minting no temp and emitting no marker. That is why `derived` is `<end>` for 424 of the 425 gap bodies.

two_classes.place_arguments (S1): single trust-ir block, no scope table, `[Const]* Call Return`, the call's result IS the returned value (or unit), every argument a block PARAMETER or a folded scalar constant. 50 of the gap's 425 bodies.
two_classes.str_literal_arguments (CF_STR): the same grammar with the producer's `global_addr`/`const`/`ptr_from_parts` `&str` chain admitted as an argument. 324 of the gap's 425 bodies — every one of them a serde `Visitor::expecting`.

exploit_wave_CF.emission: per planned argument in operand order: built's own `StorageLive(t); t = &(*_p)` / `t = &mut (*_p)` / `t = copy _p`, and for a `&str` literal `StorageLive(t); StorageLive(u); u = const "lit"; t = &(*u)`; retired at position 0 of the call's SUCCESSOR block, argument temps in REVERSE operand order and then the literal locals.
exploit_wave_CF.gates: the wave-MF scope firewall; a source-side HIR/typeck gate that independently witnesses one `as_temp` temp per non-literal argument (`hir_params_are_simple_bindings`, a statement-free body block, a bare-path-or-literal argument list, and the `[Deref(Builtin), Borrow(Ref)]` reborrow adjustment pair); a repeated argument is refused (built mints TWO temps for one value); the emitter re-checks `route_to_ret` and the exact argument type before minting.
exploit_wave_CF.law: `mf_gate::predict_call` derives the whole marker sequence from the sealed plan and the trust-ir; `mf_gate::observe` derives it from the finished MIR. The two must be equal or the body fails closed. Beyond that the ORACLE (`mir_differential::canon_markers`) compares the derived sequence against rustc's OWN `mir_built` body and reads no plan — so a WRONG plan costs flips and cannot ship a wrong sequence at -O.
exploit_wave_CF.predicted_ceiling: if every one of the 374 passes the oracle, -O3 codegen flips go 182 -> 556 (the whole-gap ceiling is 182 -> 606).
exploit_wave_CF.risk: the emission ADDS statements to the derived body, so a body whose built MIR does not have the modelled shape loses its `agreed` verdict and its -O0 flip too. Blast radius measured: 0 of the S1 bodies currently carry `markers_exact`, and 0 currently flip at -O3, so no existing green can be lost at -O3; the -O0 side is the exposure and is what the measurement has to report.

THE_SECOND_WALL.headline: The marker gate is 100% of the -O0/-O3 GAP. It is NOT the whole COST of closing it.
THE_SECOND_WALL.finding: Give a gap body an exact marker sequence and it does not flip: it hits `local type outside fragment: &'{erased} T`, the flip's own fragment check, which refuses a derived body that DECLARES a reference-typed local. That is exactly what built's argument temp is, and it is why the wave-8a forward existed. 16 of the 19 bodies whose markers were fixed died there; 2 survived, and both are the by-value-scalar shape that mints no reference local.
THE_SECOND_WALL.consequence_for_the_ceiling: the +424 marker ceiling is real for `markers_exact` and NOT reachable for FLIPS without also widening the fragment. Measured on the argument-type census of the 50-body S1 class: 48 pass at least one pointer argument and 2 do not — so ~4% of the class converts on markers alone.
THE_SECOND_WALL.the_next_build_item_stated_precisely: admit a reference-typed local into the flip fragment when it is (a) minted by a marker plan, (b) initialized by `Rvalue::Ref` of a deref of a PARAMETER place, and (c) consumed exactly once, as a bare `Operand::Move` argument of the call terminator in the same block. Every one of those three is already checked by `plan_call_fwd_markers` + the emitter; what is missing is the fragment gate being told.
